title: Refactor gateway credit decoupling and fncall writer throttles
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Decouple route credit accounting from proxy write buffers to improve streaming stability; introduce per-route fncall writer throttles and a minimal stream buffer configuration to reduce tail latency for streaming toolcalls. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: streaming instability and occasional toolcall stalls during bursty writes are caused by tight coupling between route credits and the proxy write buffer. This PR separates credit accounting from IO buffering, adds a small deterministic write buffer floor, and introduces per-route fncall_writer throttles (soft backpressure tokens) to avoid head-of-line blocking for other streams. Changes: refactor credit manager to expose a decoupled credit reservation API; add StreamBufferManager with configurable min_stream_buffer_bytes and per-route soft_limit_ms; implement FncallWriterThrottle that uses leaky-bucket smoothing and hedging for slow clients; route-level config flags to opt-in for aggressive buffering on legacy routes; compatibility shim for OpenAI-compat that preserves existing handshake semantics while using new buffering logic. Tests & validation: unit tests for credit edge-cases, integration tests simulating slow TCP drains, synthetic perf runs showing tail-latency improvements, and a gradual canary rollout plan. Checklist: [x] refactor credit model [x] implement buffer manager [x] fncall throttle + hedging [x] add metrics/traces [x] e2e tests + canary rollout. Rollout plan: staged rollout to 10% gateway nodes, monitor token-drop and stream-latency dashboards for 48h, expand to 50% if no regressions, full rollout after two successful expansion steps.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain why the min_stream_buffer_bytes default is 16KB? Is that empirically tuned?
Aisha Patel: We picked 16KB after microbenchmarks on 4xV100 clusters; it balances kernel write overhead and latency. Added benchmark numbers to docs/gateway-buffering.md.
Sofia Alvarez: Concern: hedging opens additional concurrent downstream requests; how do we bound client-side amplification?

Aisha Patel: Hedging is limited to one extra speculative write per route and only triggers when the writer queue latency exceeds soft_limit_ms. Added a circuit-breaker that disables hedging if amplification > 1.5x over window.
Ethan Brooks: Integration tests flaky locally (slow_drain test fails intermittently). Can we stabilize?
Aisha Patel: Fixed race in the test harness and added deterministic drain timing; e2e run in CI now passes consistently.
